newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - CSX sees record Q4 net, EPS.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - CSX sees record Q4 net, EPS.

text.p: CSX Corp chairman John Snow said the company expects to report record net income and earnings per share for the fourth quarter.
In a telephone interview, Snow also said he is comfortable with Wall Street earnings estimates of $1.14 per share.
"That's in the ballpark. We'd be comfortable with that," he said.
CSX is expected to report fourth quarter earnings next week.

For the company's railroad unit, which also is expected to post a record quarter, Snow described traffic as "reasonably strong". He noted that weakness in merchandise shipments and unexpectedly high fuel costs were offset by strength in coal, which is the railroad's biggest commodity.
Expense reductions also helped the bottom line, he said.
"All in all, I'd say the railroad performed extraordinarily well and continued (its) string of new record years and new record quarters," he said.
The Sea-Land shipping unit will report a "reasonably strong" quarter in excess of the year-ago period, Snow said.
Sea-Land volumes rose in the fourth quarter, but rates remained below year-ago level, keeping revenues at or slightly below fourth quarter 1995, Snow said.
Snow said the rate pressure that hurt Sea-Land throughout 1996 should ease in 1997.

"We think the rates will still be under pressure, but a lot of the excess capacity will be worked off over the course of the year...While rates will not be restored to former levels, I don't think we'll see anywhere near as negative a rate environment as we saw last year," he said, noting much of the rate pressure was in the Pacific.
Rates also are improving for the intermodal operations, Snow said.

"Our fourth quarter is going to show some nice improvement over the fourth quarter of last year, which means we're starting to get back on track for fairly strong earnings at the intermodal company," he said.
